text: Describe the factors considered by the court when deciding whether a duty of care should be
imposed for a negligent misstatement. Assess the effectiveness of these factors. [25]
Different levels of protection should be afforded to certain categories of visitor in the context of the
Occupiers’ Liability Act 1957.
Describe the duty owed to visitors and assess the validity of the statement above. [25]
Explain the defence of contributory negligence and assess whether it achieves fairness between
claimants and defendants. [25]
Section B
John has worked for AB Paints Ltd (ABP) for over 20 years. He has recently been diagnosed with
a rare and serious illness. He believes that this may have been caused by exposure to a specific
chemical used in the manufacturing process.
His doctor has informed John that there was significant research published 10 years ago
connecting this chemical to the type of illness with which he has been diagnosed. John is now
unable to work and is facing very significant costs for his medical treatment. He believes that ABP
has been aware of the risks highlighted by the research since its publication.
John’s colleague, Bill, has also worked for ABP for 20 years. He has not been diagnosed with any
physical condition but he has been unable to work since John’s diagnosis. He is depressed due to
the worry that he too may develop this illness.
Advise the parties as to their rights and liabilities in relation to negligence in this situation. [25]
Steve attends the annual Barchester firework display with a group of classmates from his college
course. One of the group, Alan, brings some small fireworks of his own. During the display, Alan
ignites one of these fireworks and throws it at the group to frighten them. As the firework is about
to hit Steve, he deflects it but it then hits a bystander, Megan, and causes her serious injuries
when it explodes.
Megan’s husband, Ian, believes that Steve threw the firework. He shouts at Steve that he will kill
him for what he has done. As Ian approaches him, Steve runs away but finds his path blocked by
a number of security guards.
Advise the parties as to their rights and liabilities in relation to trespass to the person in this
situation. [25]
Tadgh has lived in a small village for many years. He works from home as an artist. The house next
door was recently purchased by Dr Smith. She and her family have moved in and she operates a
medical clinic from the ground floor.
The clinic is very busy and Tadgh is finding it difficult to concentrate on his work due to the noise
of patients and their vehicles arriving at and leaving the clinic. On a number of occasions, patients
have parked on his driveway. He has asked Dr Smith to address these issues but nothing has
changed.
th
Last week, Dr Smith hosted a party for her daughter’s 18 birthday. There was a band playing
loud music with a lightshow in the garden. Tadgh complained about the noise at 23:30 but the loud
music and the party continued until 04:00.
The day after the party, Tadgh purchased a drum kit and is now practising for several hours every
day. Dr Smith has asked him to stop as it is interfering with the work of the clinic but Tadgh has
ignored her request.
Advise the parties as to their rights and remedies in relation to private nuisance in this situation.
